<description>
`ChainstateManager` creates and owns its `BlockManager`, which means block storage can't exist without chainstate management. #35627 discussed moving that ownership out of `ChainstateManager`, and the kernel needs it to configure, read and prune block storage on its own.

`NodeContext` and the kernel now create the `BlockManager` first, pass it to `ChainstateManager` by reference and destroy `ChainstateManager` first.

The first commit makes the kernel's `ChainMan` destroy its `ChainstateManager` explicitly. On master `ChainMan` declares its context last, which destroys the context before the `ChainstateManager` that refers into it. Nothing reads through those references during teardown, so this changes no behavior, but the order no longer depends on how the members are declared.

The last commit removes `ChainstateLoadOptions::prune`. It duplicated the `BlockManager`'s prune mode, and the kernel never set it. Once the kernel can prune (#36856), that would make it refuse to reopen a data directory it had pruned.

The only behavior change to my knowledge is startup log order, because the block tree database opens before the script verification threads start.

An earlier version of this PR also moved `ImportBlocks` and replaced `BlockManager`'s friend declarations. I've taken them out as they're not relevant to this, but I think together better suited for a change that removes the `node/blockstorage -> validation` circular dependency (#36858)

The kernel side is #36854.
</description>

[2026-11-26] r:6074688107 review COMMENTED by musaHaruna (contributor):
Concept ACK.

This follows the ownership split we discussed in [#35627](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35627): the caller owns `BlockManager`, and `ChainstateManager` borrows it. I think this is a useful first step toward separating storage from validation.

Could we cover this in `feature_pruning.py`, at the end of `manual_test`?

```diff
-        # stop node, start back up with auto-prune at 550 MiB, make sure still runs
-        self.restart_node(node_number, extra_args=["-prune=550"])
+        self.stop_node(node_number)
+        node.assert_start_raises_init_error(
+            extra_args=["-prune=0"],
+            expected_msg="You need to rebuild the database using -reindex to go back to unpruned mode."
+            f"  This will redownload the entire blockchain.{os.linesep}"
+            "Please restart with -reindex or -reindex-chainstate to recover.",
+        )
+        self.start_node(node_number, extra_args=["-prune=550"])
```
[2026-11-26] rc:4708812319 inline on src/validation.cpp by musaHaruna (contributor):
Could we drop the separate interrupt argument and use `blockman.m_interrupt`? Current callers already share the same signal, but the constructor allows different ones.

For example, if only storage’s signal is interrupted, block-index loading can return `false` because it was asked to stop. The chainstate loader then checks `chainman.m_interrupt`. If that separate signal is still clear, it reports “Error loading block database”, even though the database is healthy.

Taking the signal from `blockman` would prevent this mismatch.

```diff
-ChainstateManager::ChainstateManager(const util::SignalInterrupt& interrupt, Options options, node::BlockManager& blockman)
+ChainstateManager::ChainstateManager(Options options, node::BlockManager& blockman)
     : m_script_check_queue{/*batch_size=*/128, std::clamp(options.worker_threads_num, 0, MAX_SCRIPTCHECK_THREADS)},
-      m_interrupt{interrupt},
+      m_interrupt{blockman.m_interrupt},
```
The declaration and callers would also need the interrupt argument removed.
